summary: Defines inetOrgPerson, an LDAP object class for describing a person in an organization's directory. It extends the X.521 organizationalPerson class with attributes commonly needed for Internet and intranet use. It is an informational memo, and later RFCs update it.

plainLanguage.summary: A company directory needs a standard form for each person. This memo defines a form with the boxes Internet directories usually need, such as an email address and a display name, so that every directory fills it in the same way.

subtitle: A standard directory entry describing a person in an organization, designed for Internet and intranet directories.

tldr.problem: The X.500 standards define many attribute types and object classes, but none describes a person well enough for Internet and intranet directory deployments.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines a structural object class, inetOrgPerson, derived from the X.521 organizationalPerson class. It adds nine new attribute types, including displayName, employeeNumber and userSMIMECertificate, and lists the other attributes the class may hold.
tldr.outcome: Using the class is optional. It is offered as a well-documented class that implementers can adopt. It is an Informational RFC that later RFCs have updated.

today: RFC 2798 is an Informational RFC. It has not been obsoleted, but it has been updated by RFC 3698, RFC 4519 and RFC 4524, so those should be read alongside it.

sections.title: Background and Intended Use
sections.content:
The inetOrgPerson object class is a general purpose class that holds attributes about people. Its attributes were chosen to fit the information needs of typical Internet and intranet directory services. It is designed for directories based on LDAP (RFC 2251) and the X.500 family of protocols, and may be useful in other settings too.

There is no requirement for implementers to use it. It is simply presented as a well-documented class they can adopt if it is useful. The definitions are written in the BNF forms of AttributeTypeDescription and ObjectClassDescription from RFC 2252. Attributes that the RFC references but does not define come from RFC 1274, RFC 2079 and RFC 2256, and an appendix summarizes every attribute type, syntax and matching rule involved.
sections.plainLanguage: It is a ready-made contact card that any organization can use if it wants, but nobody is forced to.

sections.title: The Nine New Attribute Types
sections.content:
Section 2 defines nine attribute types that are new to this class: carLicense, departmentNumber, displayName, employeeNumber, employeeType, jpegPhoto, preferredLanguage, userSMIMECertificate and userPKCS12.

A few choices are worth noting. displayName exists because other name attributes such as cn can hold several values, so an entry needs one name chosen for one-line summary lists. employeeType typically holds values such as Contractor, Employee, Intern, Temp, External and Unknown, though any value is allowed. preferredLanguage values must follow the Accept-Language syntax of RFC 2068, with the header name and colon left out. jpegPhoto stores JPEG images; the RFC notes that no referencable definition of that attribute could be located.

The two certificate attributes are stored and requested in binary form, as userSMIMECertificate;binary and userPKCS12;binary. The S/MIME attribute holds a PKCS#7 SignedData carrying the person's certificate chain, and when it is available it is preferred over userCertificate for S/MIME applications.
sections.plainLanguage: The new boxes on the form are things like a name to show on screen, an employee number, a photo, and a language the person prefers.

sections.title: The inetOrgPerson Object Class
sections.content:
inetOrgPerson represents people who are associated with an organization in some way. It is a structural class with object identifier 2.16.840.1.113730.3.2.2, derived from the X.521 organizationalPerson class.

Its own attribute list is entirely optional (MAY) and covers things such as mail, uid, mobile, homePhone, manager, secretary and labeledURI, together with the nine new types. Inherited from organizationalPerson and person are three required attributes, cn, objectClass and sn, plus many optional ones including telephoneNumber, title and userPassword.
sections.plainLanguage: The form builds on the basic person form and adds optional boxes. Only a common name and a family name are required.

sections.title: An Example Entry
sections.content: The RFC gives an example entry for a person named Barbara Jensen, written in LDIF. It names the entry with a distinguished name, lists the object classes top, person, organizationalPerson and inetOrgPerson, and fills in values such as two cn values, a displayName, a title, phone numbers, a carLicense, a departmentNumber and a preferredLanguage. The example shows how the inherited and the new attributes sit together in a single entry.
sections.plainLanguage: The example is one filled-in form for a make-believe person, showing how all the boxes look when used.

sections.title: Privacy and Password Cautions
sections.content: The security section is brief. Directory attributes describe real-world objects, which can be people, organizations or devices, and most countries have privacy laws about publishing information about people. The RFC also strongly discourages sending cleartext passwords where the transport cannot guarantee confidentiality, because that can reveal the password to unauthorized parties.
sections.plainLanguage: A directory full of personal details deserves care: do not share people's information needlessly, and do not say passwords out loud where others can hear.

items.label: Vehicle plate
items.desc: Vehicle license or registration plate; multivalued.

items.label: Department
items.desc: Identifies a department within an organization.

items.label: Display name
items.desc: Preferred name to use when displaying entries; single-valued.

items.label: Employee type
items.desc: Type of employment, such as Contractor or Intern.

items.label: Photo
items.desc: One or more JPEG images of a person.

items.label: Language
items.desc: Preferred written or spoken language; single-valued.

items.label: S/MIME certificate
items.desc: PKCS#7 SignedData used to support S/MIME.

items.label: PKCS #12
items.desc: PFX PDU for exchange of personal identity information.
